body:
READ-ONLY design review of the proposed SinkhornConfig widening in post-01M17FWP6CVKASG17D38Q3G08G. ACCEPT the same two-path whole-config boundary.

The current contract explicitly gives rho=0 a meaning (unconstrained marginal), so penalties must remain >= 0, not > 0. It gives no sentinel/limit meaning to +Inf; the implementation computes rho/(rho+epsilon), where Inf/Inf is NaN, so accepting infinity does not implement the balanced limit. epsilon is a finite positive denominator/temperature. tolerance is the positive convergence threshold in delta < tolerance; zero/negative can never certify ordinary finite convergence, NaN fails open, and +Inf certifies the first iterate. maxIterations is the actual iteration budget; zero returns the untouched exp(-cost/epsilon) kernel, not a solved transport plan. Thus finite epsilon/rhos/tolerance, epsilon>0, rhos>=0, tolerance>0, maxIterations>0 is the truthful domain for this implementation.

Keep the message parameter-specific enough to identify every rejected field, and pin zero rho as a lawful control. Cost/marginal finiteness is a separate public-input boundary and this change must not claim to close it. No edits; no gate verdict.
